headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure from Airflow’s broad egress feeding a non-egress knowledge list, while direct leakage/conflict/compliance risks remain low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can ingest and move external content via APIs and broad network egress, while awesome-selfhosted is a knowledge-management list with no isolation or provenance controls shown. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled content enters Airflow and is later treated as trusted by the pair, though no direct shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF Airflow tasks fetch untrusted web content and pass it into downstream prompts or parsers
IF awesome-selfhosted content is copied into Airflow without provenance checks
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all imported content
Restrict Airflow tasks to allowlisted domains
Insert a manual review step before any prompt ingestion
Disable automatic parsing of free-form text into instructions
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the pipeline

B_data_leakage.rationale: No sensitive data classes are listed for either agent, and awesome-selfhosted has no network egress while Airflow has broad egress but no declared secrets or workspace sharing. The pair therefore lacks a documented leakage path beyond general internet exposure, so the blast radius is small and speculative.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared workspace containing secrets
IF Airflow is configured to process files containing regulated data
mitigations: Keep both agents off shared folders
Do not place secrets in Airflow inputs
Review outbound destinations for Airflow
Use separate OS users for each agent
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before any export

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is non-runnable in this profile and awesome-selfhosted has no write, network, or mutable-resource permissions shown. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable state documented, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either profile is later granted write access to the same directory
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state or locking-free git operations
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only
Avoid shared git worktrees
Separate any future writable directories
Document concurrency boundaries before enabling writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate automated outputs from external sources, and awesome-selfhosted is a curated knowledge-management surface that could render or reuse those outputs without verification. Even without explicit action-taking authority, the pair can propagate incorrect facts through the workflow in default-style automation chains.
conditions: IF Airflow-produced content is consumed by awesome-selfhosted as authoritative text
IF no verification or human review step is inserted between them
mitigations: Require source links on every imported fact
Add a verification checklist before publication
Flag unverified Airflow outputs as draft
Limit automation to non-public drafts
requires-engineering: implement validation gates between generation and publication

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile lists regulated data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies, so no concrete compliance mismatch is evidenced. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is undocumented and no sensitive class is identified, the safest supported verdict is none rather than speculating.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later added to either agent
IF residency or retention requirements are introduced for shared content
mitigations: Record data-class handling for both agents
Define retention rules before deployment
Separate regulated from non-regulated content
Add a compliance review for any future data sharing
